sampler_discrepancy.observation: In both runs, the --rss-samples 1 Hz VmRSS series stays flat near baseline (~170-196 MB) for the entire 120 s run, while /usr/bin/time -v's lifetime 'Maximum resident set size' for the same process is ~1.9-2.0 GB.
sampler_discrepancy.interpretation: Most consistent with a fast-appearing, fast-receding native-heap allocation spike (e.g. large glibc mmap-backed allocations made and munmap'd within a sub-second window, or per-thread malloc-arena churn across the 64 client threads) rather than a value that climbs and holds steady across the step -- exactly the kind of native-allocator behavior the P-OV1 README already flagged as invisible to tracemalloc, and it turns out to be coarse-grained-RSS-polling-invisible too. Pinning the exact allocation site would need finer-grained sampling (e.g. 100 ms VmRSS polling, or mallinfo2()/malloc_stats() snapshots) -- out of scope for this bounded diagnostic and left as a follow-up.
sampler_discrepancy.does_not_change_the_verdict: This affects only the --rss-samples time series' usefulness for localizing WHEN the spike happens; the --no-call-records ablation below is a between-run comparison of /usr/bin/time -v's peak (a full-process, allocator-visible measurement in both runs), which is unaffected by the polling gap.

verdict_v1_superseded_2026_09_15.status: HELD by the coordinator -- see hwm_checkpoint_followup_v2 and the amended top-level verdict below. Kept verbatim for the record, not because it is now believed correct as stated.
verdict_v1_superseded_2026_09_15.reasoning: Disabling the harness's own per-call retention entirely (--no-call-records: no CallRecord list, no 76,800-entry .records.json written) changed the process's peak RSS by about 0.6% (1,991,888 KB with records vs 2,004,096 KB without -- the no-call-records run is if anything slightly HIGHER, within run-to-run noise). If the multi-GB growth were harness-side bookkeeping (the CallRecord list plus its end-of-sweep JSON serialization, as the P-OV1 tracemalloc note suspected but could not confirm past ~83 MB), removing that retention should have collapsed the peak toward the ~150-200 MB baseline seen in the low-rate/1-client steps. It did not. Both peaks are two orders of magnitude above what tracemalloc's harness-side accounting could ever explain (it only ever attributed ~83 MB), and now also above what removing that accounting removes (~0 MB of the ~2 GB). The growth is therefore attributable to something outside scripts/eval_overload.py's own Python-level bookkeeping -- most plausibly the native engine (tgms._engine, a Rust .so) or glibc allocator behavior triggered by 64 concurrently-calling threads hammering ToolRouter/ConcurrencyGate at once, not Python-level result retention by either class (grep of tgms/tools/server.py and tgms/tools/limits.py finds no accumulating list/history field on ToolRouter or ConcurrencyGate -- neither class retains past call results, so 'result retention' in the literal sense is also ruled out as the mechanism, leaving native-heap/allocator behavior under thread concurrency as the leading candidate).
verdict_v1_superseded_2026_09_15.not_pinned_down: This diagnostic identifies WHERE the growth is not (harness CallRecord retention, ToolRouter/ConcurrencyGate result history, the edge-postings index, the byte-budget segment cache) but does not identify the exact native allocation site -- that would need native-side profiling (e.g. Valgrind/massif, jemalloc/glibc arena instrumentation, or per-thread RSS breakdown) against tgms._engine, which is out of scope for this bounded (~10 min) measurement.
verdict_v1_superseded_2026_09_15.why_held: The coordinator flagged that /usr/bin/time -v reports a process-LIFETIME peak, while the 1 Hz --rss-samples series sat at ~190 MB throughout the 64-client step -- so the ~2 GB could belong to a pre-step phase (store copy/upgrade-manifests/open) rather than to the service under load, which this run's between-run comparison alone could not distinguish.

One bounded run, --no-call-records, otherwise identical protocol to the v1 no-call-records run above (fresh synth-1m-native copy, upgrade-manifests format 1->3 generation 21 sha e7f45e1257dd14c8 -- identical, confirming the same store state; REPLAY-2 pid 2453943 confirmed running concurrently throughout, CPU 89.8%, RSS ~2.1 GB; OSV poller pid 1457823 and daily loop pid 1540052 untouched).

hwm_checkpoint_followup_v2.hwm_checkpoints_note: VmHWM only ever increases within a process's life, so a checkpoint's value already reflects any peak reached up to that point even if RSS later receded -- it cannot miss a spike the way a VmRSS poll can. after_store_open == before_step_n64 (99,488 KB): building the ToolRouter/Limits/ConcurrencyGate over an already-open store costs essentially nothing. after_step_n64 is 226,928 KB -- 2.3x the post-open baseline, but nowhere near the ~2 GB process lifetime peak.

ten_hz_rss_sampler_peak.note: 863 samples over the full ~150 s run (load:64 then recovery); flat at ~194,772 kB for the entire recovery portion checked (from t=133.988s onward) -- the 10x faster sampling still shows no spike anywhere near 2 GB, consistent with the after_step_n64 HWM checkpoint

hwm_checkpoint_followup_v2.localization: Neither store open (99,488 KB) nor the n_clients=64 step itself, up to and including the moment all 64 client threads join (226,928 KB HWM) accounts for the ~2 GB peak -- both are now ruled OUT as the growth's location, contradicting both the original v1 framing ('the step under load') and the coordinator's alternative hypothesis ('pre-step phases: store copy/upgrade-manifests/open'). Since VmHWM cannot decrease, the ~1.79 GB gap between after_step_n64 (226,928 KB) and the process's final peak (2,016,400 KB) must open during the remainder of the run: the recovery step (1 client, 20 Hz, ~60 s) and/or the final teardown (store.digest(), store.close(), writing the manifest/records files, interpreter shutdown). The 10 Hz RSS series covers that remainder too and stays flat there as well, so whatever is responsible is invisible to VmRSS polling at both 1 Hz and 10 Hz -- same blind spot as the v1 sampler_discrepancy, now narrowed to a smaller window but not yet resolved to a single phase.
hwm_checkpoint_followup_v2.not_yet_checkpointed: This run only added the four checkpoints the coordinator asked for. A fifth (after the recovery step, immediately before store.close()) and a sixth (immediately before process exit) would split the remaining ~1.79 GB between 'recovery step' and 'teardown/shutdown' -- left as the next bounded step, not run here to keep this measurement to its ~10 min budget.

verdict_v2_superseded_2026_09_15.answer: HELD/AMENDED, 2026-09-15: not resolved to 'service under 64-client load' or 'harness bookkeeping' as originally framed -- both are narrowed but the growth's phase is now known more precisely, and it is NOT where either original hypothesis placed it.
verdict_v2_superseded_2026_09_15.status: SUPERSEDED by hwm_checkpoint_pinning_v3 below, which adds the two checkpoints this verdict names as missing and pins the phase directly. Kept verbatim for the record.
verdict_v2_superseded_2026_09_15.reasoning: The HWM-checkpoint run rules out two candidates directly: (1) store open/upgrade-manifests footprint -- only 99,488 KB, not ~1.9 GB, so the coordinator's 'startup/open footprint' hypothesis is refuted; (2) the n_clients=64 step's own execution -- VmHWM right after all 64 client threads join is only 226,928 KB, and VmHWM cannot decrease, so the step itself never drove RSS anywhere near 2 GB while its threads were alive. That also means the v1 --no-call-records ablation's conclusion ('service surface under load') needs qualification: the ablation correctly shows the ~2 GB is not the harness's CallRecord list (removing it didn't move the peak), but the HWM checkpoints now show it isn't happening DURING the load step's threads either -- it opens later, in the recovery step and/or store.digest()/store.close()/teardown, a phase neither v1 run instrumented and which the 1 Hz AND 10 Hz RSS pollers both still fail to see (flat throughout). So: harness per-call bookkeeping remains ruled out (unchanged from v1); 'growth under 64-client load, visible while the load is applied' is now also ruled out; the leading candidate shifts to store/engine teardown (store.digest()/store.close()) or the low-rate recovery step, still on the service/native side (not eval_overload.py's own retained state), but not yet the specific location v1 implied.
verdict_v2_superseded_2026_09_15.next_step_not_taken_here: Two more HWM checkpoints (after the recovery step; immediately before process exit) would attribute the remaining ~1.79 GB to 'recovery step' vs. 'teardown' directly. Not run in this pass to hold to the bounded measurement budget -- recorded as the concrete next step rather than left implicit.

hwm_checkpoint_pinning_v3.pinned_phase: store.digest() (Store.digest(), tgms/store.py -> StorageAdapter.store_digest(), tgms/storage/base.py). VmHWM is flat at 227,280 KB through after_step_n64 AND after_recovery_step (the recovery step adds exactly 0 KB), then jumps by 1,772,688 KB (227,280 -> 1,999,968) at the single after_store_digest_full checkpoint, then stays flat through after_store_close and before_exit (0 KB added by either). No other single call in the run's remaining lifetime touches HWM at all -- the coordinator's hypothesis is confirmed exactly: store_digest() (tgms/storage/base.py) builds `sorted((v.to_json() for v in self.all_node_versions()), ...)` and the same for edges -- materializing every node/edge version row into a Python list before hashing -- so its peak scales with total row count, not with anything the 64-client load actually did.
hwm_checkpoint_pinning_v3.not_service_under_load: This retroactively corrects both the v1 and v2 framing: the ~1.9-2.0 GB is not the service surface responding to concurrent load (ToolRouter/ConcurrencyGate/native engine during the 64-client step) and not the recovery step either -- it is the harness's own end-of-sweep bookkeeping call (`store_digest = store.digest()` in `scripts/eval_overload.py::run_sweep`), made once per sweep regardless of how many clients or calls preceded it. In that specific sense the v1 '--no-call-records didn't move the peak, so it's not harness bookkeeping' conclusion was right about CallRecord retention but wrong about the mechanism being outside the harness's control -- digest() is a harness-side finalization step, just not the one v1 tested.

verdict.answer: PINNED, 2026-09-15: the ~1.9-2.0 GB lifetime peak is `Store.digest()`, called once at the end of scripts/eval_overload.py::run_sweep to populate the manifest's dataset digest -- not the service surface under 64-client load, not the recovery step, and not per-call harness bookkeeping (CallRecord retention).
verdict.service_surface_hwm_through_the_step: 227,280 KB (≈227 MB, after_step_n64 and after_recovery_step -- identical) -- this is the true footprint of ToolRouter/ConcurrencyGate/the native engine actually serving 76,800 calls at max_concurrent=8 plus a 1200-call recovery step. It is flat, small, and unremarkable.
verdict.lifetime_peak_belongs_to: store.digest() -- confirmed by a direct before/after checkpoint straddling the single call, not inferred from a polling gap: 227,280 KB immediately before, 1,999,968 KB immediately after, no further growth through close()/exit.
verdict.fix: Store.digest_streaming() (tgms/store.py -> StorageAdapter.store_digest_streaming(), tgms/storage/base.py), merged to main via the B7a streaming-digest work (commits c5c03a9/3731a67, merge 4930213) after this lane's branch point (23bf664) -- proved byte-identical to Store.digest() in tests/test_store_digest_streaming.py, and bounded-memory by construction (an external merge sort over chunk_rows-sized spilled batches instead of materializing every row). scripts/eval_overload.py now takes an additive --digest-mode {full,streaming} flag (default 'full', unchanged behaviour) that calls digest_streaming() instead when set to 'streaming'; on a checkout that lacks it (this lane's own branch included, since it predates the merge) it raises a clear RuntimeError naming the missing method and the commits that add it, rather than silently falling back to 'full' and mislabeling the manifest. --digest-mode is recorded in every manifest's config for provenance. Not exercised live in this diagnostic (this branch doesn't have digest_streaming yet); the fix is landed in the harness and ready to flip once this lane rebases onto or merges a main that includes it.
verdict.not_pinned_down: Why store_digest() costs ~1.77 GB specifically for this store (row count, per-row JSON overhead, the sort's own temporary lists) is not measured here -- only that the call is the single location of the growth. The B7a commit message already gives an approximate figure for a different store size (17.4M-edge store: 25 GB), consistent in direction with this store's smaller ~1.77 GB for ~1M rows.
